cards.text: Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, just went to war alongside Ahab, king of Israel, and Ahab didn't make it home. Jehoshaphat did. He's back in Jerusalem, safe.
He's home, and who goes out to confront him? Jehu son of Hanani the seer, and friend, that man did NOT bring a welcome-home cookie box.

cards.question: Jehu goes out to confront King Jehoshaphat. What does Jehu call him out for?
Because Jehoshaphat helped the wicked and loved those who hate the LORD, Jehu says the ___ of the LORD is upon him.
Jehu tells Jehoshaphat that some good is found in him too.
What good does Jehu say Jehoshaphat has done in the land?

answers.text: He fed the hungry in Judah

cards.text: Jehu adds that Jehoshaphat has set his heart on seeking God. That's your boss saying "We need to talk" and then "Also, GREAT work this year" in the same meeting.
Jehoshaphat lives in Jerusalem, and once again he goes out among the people. From Beersheba ALL the way up to the hill country of Ephraim.

cards.question: As Jehoshaphat goes out among the people from Beersheba to Ephraim, what does he do?

answers.text: Turns them back to the LORD

cards.text: Next he appoints judges in each of the fortified cities of Judah. Then he gives them a word: consider carefully what you do.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat tells the new judges they are not judging for man, but for the ___.

cards.text: The LORD is with them when they render judgment, he says. So may the fear of the LORD be upon them, and they'd better be careful what they do.

cards.question: Jehoshaphat tells the judges to be careful. What reason does he give about the LORD?

answers.text: With the LORD there is no partiality or bribery
The LORD will remove any judge who slips up
The LORD writes down every ruling they make

cards.text: Nobody's getting off with a cookie box under the table. Not even mine, and baker, mine are GOOD. Then Jehoshaphat appoints judges in Jerusalem too, to judge on behalf of the LORD and settle disputes.

cards.question: Who does Jehoshaphat appoint to judge in Jerusalem?

answers.text: Levites and priests and family heads

cards.text: He charges them to serve faithfully and wholeheartedly in the fear of the LORD. Disputes will come to them from their brothers in the cities, about bloodshed or some other violation of the law.

cards.question: When a dispute comes from their brothers in the cities, Jehoshaphat tells the Jerusalem judges to warn them.
Why does Jehoshaphat want the Jerusalem judges to warn the people who bring disputes?

answers.text: So they won't incur guilt before the LORD
So the courts won't get too crowded
So the king won't have to hear about it

cards.question: Jehoshaphat names who's over the judges. Amariah the chief priest is over all that pertains to the ___, and Zebadiah son of Ishmael, ruler of the house of Judah, is over all that pertains to the ___.

cards.text: The Levites will serve as officers, and Jehoshaphat sends them off with this: "Act resolutely; may the LORD be with the upright!" We'll leave King Jehoshaphat right there for now, friend, but his story is still in the oven.

findings.problem: The question includes "not judging for man," which rules out both wrong answers. "people" and "king" are both men, so the only answer left is "LORD." The baker can get it right from the wording, without understanding the passage.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer ("With the LORD there is no partiality or bribery") uses the passage's formal wording. The wrong answers sound casual and modern, especially "slips up," so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
